text:
Jess: Heads-up — hit a weird latency spike on the LL128 rollout for seq_len=2048 KV-cache workloads. saw heavy allreduce tailing and a couple of NCCL WARNs. samples attached below.

Aryan: ugh. is this on the 8xA100 pool or the 4xA10 test rig?

Jess: 8xA100 (nvlink mesh). repro on dedicated staging. initial spike happens ~60s after sustained traffic, looks like algorithm fallback.

Kwon: can you paste the NCCL logs? those WARN messages are telling.

Jess: sure — snippet from the runtime agent logs (trimmed):
```
NCCL WARN Call to ncclCommInitRank failed, trying fallback
NCCL INFO using algorithm LL128 for 98% of ops
NCCL WARN small op detected, switching to RING algo for allreduce
allreduce time: 3.2ms -> 12.9ms (per-step)
kv-cache writeback chunk_size=512kb, batch=32
```

Liana: interesting — the runtime's chunking means larger payloads cross a threshold and push the collective into a RING path. that kills bandwidth on mesh NVLink.

Aryan: i ran a micro-run earlier and saw the same pattern. when we force NCCL_ALGO=LL128 + NCCL_PROTO=LL we avoid fallback but latency variance goes up with bigger chunks. smaller chunk sizes reduce variance but increase CPU overhead.

Kwon: do we have telemetry linkage between sequence length distribution and allreduce size? could be KV cache flushing more entries when sequence grows.

Jess: yep — correlates with long-tail sequences from a small user cohort. KV cache prefetch adapter writes ~1.2MB per shard every few steps. combined with channel count=4 seems to saturate a link and then NCCL falls back.

perf-bot: Automated alert: perf/regression/ll128_fallback — 8% p95 latency increase over last deploy (run id: 2026-03-17_17). Link: https://perf.redwood/ll128_fallback

Liana: candidate fixes: 1) increase channels to spread chunking, 2) reduce KV chunk size for seq>1024, 3) tweak NCCL_TOPO or NCCL_ALGO settings per-pool.

Aryan: also try NCCL_COLLNET_DISABLE=1? on non-collnet hw that sometimes forces better tree/ring behavior. but careful.

Kwon: i'd like to quantify comm/compute overlap impact. can we run with perf-harness flag `--trace-collect=cuda,nccl,host` and a controlled load (seq=2048, batch=8) and compare: channels=4 vs channels=8 vs channels=2, and NCCL_ALGO forced vs auto.

Jess: i'll kick that off. shard of commands i'm using:
```
# repro harness
python tools/perf_harness.py --model rtrk-small --seq 2048 --batch 8 --clients 16 \
  --nccl-env "NCCL_ALGO=LL128;NCCL_PROTO=LL;NCCL_NTHREADS=8" --channels 4
```

Liana: nice. add `--kv-chunk-size=256kb` for one run. also collect `nvprof --profile-from-start off --print-gpu-trace` or Nsight to get overlap numbers.

Aryan: quick numbers from my earlier run: channels=4, auto-algo -> p50/p95 tokens: 18ms / 62ms. channels=8, force-ll128 -> 16ms / 34ms. channels=8 but kv-chunk=256k -> 15ms / 28ms.

Kwon: substantial. suggests increasing channel parallelism helps reduce probability of fallback and improves overlap. but we need guardrails: more channels = more memory and scheduling overhead.

Jess: plan: run 3 full sweeps (channels 2/4/8) with trace, attach nvlink counters, and collect a subset of requests to identify sequences that trigger the fallback. i'll post artifacts here.

perf-bot: Job 4521 queued: perf-harness (channels sweep). ETA ~18m.

Liana: after results, we'll pick a conservative default: channels=6 for 8xA100, kv-chunk cap at 512kb, and a runtime check to drop to ring only when ops below threshold. we should also add a regression test in CI to fail if auto-fallback rate > 1% on synthetic long-seq workload.

Aryan: agree. also let's try toggling NCCL_ALGO=RING for one run to get a baseline worst-case.

Jess: OK — kicking jobs now. will update with traces + a short summary (numbers + recommended config change) once done. :coffee:

Kwon: thanks — if you see any `NCCL COMM ERR` please ping on pager.

Liana: gl.
